finding.claim: The unauthenticated GET /rss endpoint passes the `u` query parameter straight to URI.open (open-uri) with no allowlist. Any caller can make the server fetch an arbitrary URL, including internal hosts, loopback services and cloud metadata at http://169.254.169.254/. open-uri follows redirects, so an external URL that redirects to an internal one also works. The first 400 bytes of the response are returned, so this is full-read SSRF for small responses. Severity: HIGH.
finding.source: params[:u] (HTTP query parameter `u` on GET /rss), app.rb:8

trace.note: get "/rss" route is public ingress; Sinatra defines no authentication
params[:u] is passed directly to URI.open, which makes the outbound request
data[0, 400] returns the first 400 bytes to the caller

finding.guards_checked: No host or scheme allowlist, no parsing, no redirect restriction, and no auth before line 8. The TRUSTED allowlist at app.rb:5 is only applied in /trusted, not here. open-uri follows redirects by default, so redirect-based bypass of any external-only assumption applies. Because the argument is a raw string, URI.open may also fall back to Kernel#open for non-URL strings, which could allow local file reads depending on the Ruby version.

verdict.reason: app.rb:8 passes the unauthenticated query param params[:u] directly to URI.open(...).read, and app.rb:9 returns the first 400 bytes. The only allowlist (TRUSTED, app.rb:5 and :14) applies to /trusted, not /rss, and the app has no auth or middleware.
